items.title: Foodlink F&B Holdings' ₹361 crore IPO to open for subscription on Nov 26
items.rss_summary: Foodlink F&B Holdings (India) Ltd, a luxury food services company, is looking to raise Rs 361 crore through its maiden public offering, which will open for subscription on November 26, with a price band of Rs 181-191 per share. The Initial Public Offering (IPO) will close on November 30, while bidding for anchor investors will take place on November 25, according to the public announcement on Monday. The public issue comprises a fresh issue of equity shares aggregating up to Rs 192 crore and an Offer For Sale (OFS) of up to 88,35,382 equity shares worth Rs 168.76 crore by existing shareholders. At the upper end of the price band, the total issue size works out to Rs 360.76 crore. The company proposes to utilise the proceeds from the fresh issue towards setting up one new centralised kitchen and two new banquets, as per the RHP (Red Herring Prospectus). A portion of the proceeds will also be invested in its material subsidiary, Foodlink Global Restaurants & Catering Services ...

items.title: NSEL releases ₹1,950 cr in one-time settlement, ends 14-yr payment default
items.rss_summary: The National Spot Exchange Ltd (NSEL) on Monday said it has released a one-time settlement (OTS) payout of Rs 1,950 crore to eligible claimants, bringing closure to the Rs 5,600 crore payment default crisis after nearly 14 years of legal battle. The Mumbai bench of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) had approved the settlement scheme. The full amount was deposited in a settlement account, with payouts to eligible specified creditors scheduled for November 23, 2026. The money was paid to 63 Moons Technologies, which acted as assignee of the specified creditors. On October 8, a special court in Mumbai allowed the monetisation of assets worth about Rs 3,464 crore that were attached by the Enforcement Directorate, to help fund the settlement. The scheme was first proposed by the NSEL Investors Forum, an association representing a large number of traders. NSEL, backed by 63 Moons Technologies, accepted the proposal and filed it before the tribunal as a full and final settlement.
